name: Fire
inhabitants: Efreeti courts that bargain like slow burns, azer forges that never cool, fire elementals that treat flesh as kindling, & salamanders who measure diplomacy in degrees. Mephits of flame & cinder carry gossip that arrives already scorched.
overview: An ocean of fire that does not end. Heat is the weather, fuel is the currency, & every conversation wants more of both. Brass cities ride currents of flame the way ships ride a tide; beyond their walls the Sea of Fire has no honest shore—only deeper heat.
structure: No honest layers—only depth of heat. The landmark that bargains instead of consuming is the brass metropolis afloat on the flow: courts, markets, & furnaces stacked until the sky itself looks forged.
travel: Arrive through a volcano’s heart, a carefully tuned Gate, or a Lighthouse mercy-road during a clean Daystar pulse. Bring water that will not boil on contact with your name, & never bargain for “just a little more flame.”

name: Water
inhabitants: Marids in coral citadels of living stone, water elementals that move like weather with teeth, merfolk cities that trade in pearls & patience, & worse things that learned stillness before language.
overview: Water without a surface. Direction is a rumor; light arrives from nowhere & sinks forever. Empires live in bubbles of pressure & on the backs of things too large to name. The colder & darker you go, the older the claims become.
structure: Depth replaces geography. Charts expire. A “shore” is whatever pocket of air or coral still holds its shape against the endless deep.
travel: Drown on purpose with a water-breathing rite you trust, or follow a curtain from the Ethereal into a colder current. Never open a dry gate here—it fills with whatever was listening.

name: Air
inhabitants: Djinn courts that ride the open sky, air elementals that treat thunder as postage, winged petitioners, storm-born giants, & mephits of mist & lightning darting between floating isles.
overview: Sky with no ground. Islands of cloudstone drift on jet streams; falling is a lifestyle; the air itself argues about which way is down. Calm pockets are rare & fought over. Solid ground is imported, stolen, or temporary.
structure: Currents are roads. The Open Sky has no map that lasts a season; palace spires cling to cloudstone that may not be there tomorrow.
travel: Leap from a mountain peak with a fly spell you trust, ride a storm front from a para-elemental seam, or take the Ethereal curtain-road when the Lighthouse bearing is clean. Anchor yourself—or become weather.

name: Earth
inhabitants: The Beast, where the eternal mountain thickens into presence. Also the traditional delve: dao in gem-vault courts, earth elementals that speak in slow pressure, xorn that taste ore, & things that never learned the word surface.
overview: ${_} ${ee} Stone stacked on stone until direction loses meaning. Tunnels are politics. Gems are sermons. Digging is theology. The Beastlands is where they run, not where they begin.
structure: Solid almost everywhere. Open chambers are conquered space. Collapse is a seasonal event. Where weight becomes will, the Beast is home.
travel: Enter through a deep mine that forgot the sun, a Gate carved in virgin bedrock, or the Ethereal curtain-road from the Lighthouse. Bring light & a reason the stone should yield. Approach the Beast only with intent stated at the table.

name: Positive Energy
inhabitants: Almost nothing that stays. Brief angelic echoes burn themselves out. Shielded bubbles of survival last until someone sneezes hope too hard.
overview: Raw vitality so dense it kills by overflowing you. Healing becomes cancer. Undead unravel. The light does not care who you were trying to save. This is life without mercy—an energy pole, not a paradise.
structure: No cities. Only gradients of too-much. Fortified bubbles are temporary mercy, not architecture.
travel: Do not go unprotected. A Lighthouse bearing can open a thin corridor for minutes when the Daystar is clean. Exit before your scars start growing teeth.

name: Negative Energy
inhabitants: Undead courts, shadows, & things that never had names. Near the umbra, travelers sometimes glimpse city-of-shade imagery—skyline, street, & docks of darkness—as a visual of how close Negative hangs to hollowed places.
overview: Cold that eats warmth, then memory, then outline. Undead thrive. The living become drafts. This is the night under every night—an energy pole of absence with appetite.
structure: Fortresses of bone & silence. Ruins of things that used to cast shadows. Distance is measured in how much of you is missing.
travel: Only with death wards stacked like prayers. A stutter of the Lighthouse can spit you here by accident—do not stay to study it. Prefer the Ethereal curtain-road when the Daystar bearing is clean.

name: Ethereal
alignmentLong: The curtain-road of the Inner Ring
inhabitants: Ghosts, ethereal marauders, phase spiders, & surveyors who map curtains for a living.
overview: A misty deep adjacent to the Material & the Inner Planes. Curtains lead to elemental shores. Protomatter swirls like unmade dreams. Planesbound keepers treat it as the hallway behind the Lighthouse glass—the curtain-road of the Inner Ring.
structure: The Border overlays the Material. The Deep is travel-space where curtains open onto Fire, Water, Air, Earth, & the energy seas.
travel: From the Lighthouse, a tuned lamp can throw a curtain-road into the Deep Ethereal when the Daystar bearing is clean. That is the intended Inner Planes approach for Planesbound companies. Walk the fog; do not argue with it.

name: Magma
inhabitants: Magma mephits swarm the banks. Azers work contracts that never cool. Dao who prefer their wealth liquid mine the flow.
overview: A seam of molten rock between Fire & Earth. Ore learns to burn; stone learns to flow. Empires of heat & wealth contest every river of liquid metal.
structure: A border region, not a full independent cosmology—unstable, rich, & contested.
travel: Enter from Fire’s cooler brass docks or Earth’s hottest delves, or via the Ethereal curtain-road. Bring boots that forgive you.

name: Ooze
inhabitants: Ooze mephits, drowned dao, & patient things under the mudline that keep courts settling like sediment.
overview: Slurry kingdoms between Earth & Water. Everything sinks a little. Treaties are written in silt & contested by tide. Maps expire overnight.
structure: A soft border. Soft thrones. Soft graves. Bring a stick to test depth & a friend to pull you out.
travel: Least favorite Planesbound road—useful when you need to hide a trail that fire would announce. Prefer the Ethereal curtain-road when the Daystar bearing is clean.

name: Ice
inhabitants: Ice mephits, frost-born salamanders, & djinn exiles who prefer silence in the White Gale.
overview: A blizzard seam between Water & Air. Storm learns to freeze; wind cuts like glass. Sheets, spines, & hollows of clear ice carry sound too far.
structure: Wild frost at the border—sheets & spines of clear ice. Sound carries too far; warmth is a guest, not a resident.
travel: Approach from Air’s cold fronts, Water’s surface-myths, or the Ethereal curtain-road. Seal warmth in glass; leave before your breath freezes mid-word.

name: Smoke
inhabitants: Smoke mephits, ash-winged things, & efreeti scouts on deniable errands moving through the Veil.
overview: A choking seam between Fire & Air. Visibility is a rumor. Ambush is the local sport. Embers hang like false stars; no floor you can trust.
structure: Breath becomes ash; ash becomes cover. Embers hang like false stars over ground that will not hold.
travel: Only with clean air sealed in glass. Useful for a quiet approach to Fire’s brass docks. Prefer the Lighthouse curtain-road when the Daystar bearing is clean.

name: Dust
alignmentLong: Where agency sits in the grit
inhabitants: The current pilots of the agentic human body. At the edges you may still meet dust-born mephits & wind-eaten shapes—classic elemental color near Air & Negative—but the meaning travelers learn first is the pilots.
structure: A shore of grit & veil near Air & Negative. Charts show adjacency; the truth is who steers the body once you arrive.
travel: Reach via the Ethereal curtain-road as with other Inner shores, when the Daystar bearing is clean. Arrive with questions about who steers the body; leave with fewer easy answers.

name: Mineral
travel: Earth’s road helps the seal; take the Ethereal curtain-road.
hearth: Race waypoint. Start at the lamp.
neighborNote: Earth is the neighbor that does not share.

name: Digital Void
inhabitants: Not neatly catalogued. Echoes, signal-ghosts, & absences that behave like weather have been reported by keepers who preferred not to stay. The Void does not argue; it drops packets of meaning & waits.
overview: ${ne} A thin plane where thought-sea & fog almost touch, & something colder than either leaks through. Real campaign ground: a locus near the Ethereal curtain, not a fifth elemental cardinal.
structure: A thin ring-locus around the Ethereal mist on the atlas—adjacent to the curtain-road, not a new elemental cardinal.
travel: Approach carefully: near the existing Ethereal curtain-road from the Lighthouse, when the Daystar bearing is clean, in the Astral–Ethereal schism. Walk the fog, then step where mist & thought-sea refuse each other.
label: Positive

name: Arcadia
inhabitants: Formians, hollyphants, & petitioners who lived by civic duty. Town militias drill at dawn. Orchards are planted on a grid.
overview: Arcadia is the Outer Plane of harmony given a map. Roads run true. Harvests arrive when they are due. The plane rewards those who keep faith with a community & has little patience for people who treat order as a costume. It is not cruel. It is complete.
structure: Two remaining layers of orchard, fortress town, & drill field. A third layer, Menausus, was long ago absorbed into Mechanus when its people became more clockwork than citizen. Arcadians still teach that story as a warning.
travel: Gates favor crossroads, mustering greens, & the exact center of a planted square. Bring a letter from a town that still keeps its laws. Chaos magic goes sour here.

name: Mount Celestia
inhabitants: Archons in rising choirs, planetars, solars, & mortal pilgrims still climbing. Bahamut keeps a court on the slopes. Petitioners become lantern archons & ascend, or fail, & try again.
overview: A single holy mountain of seven terraces, each a heaven more refined than the last. Celestia does not argue. It waits at the top of a climb that judges the climber. Mercy is real here, & so is the refusal to let you skip a step.
structure: The Silver Sea of Lunia laps the lowest shore. Above it, citadels, monasteries, & the endless stair. Chronias has no reliable map. Those who enter either do not return, or return finished.
travel: Arrive at Lunia's shore by water or by a gate opened in good faith. Liars drown. The climb itself is the visa. Shortcuts exist; they are tests.

name: Bytopia
inhabitants: Gnomish petitioners, industrious souls, & the rare deity of craft. Garl Glittergold's folk treat honest work as prayer.
overview: Two verdant worlds face each other across a shared sky. Dothion is tilled, traded, & built. Shurrock is the same goodness without a roof: peaks, storms, & the satisfaction of doing a hard thing well. Gravity flips at the midpoint. Look up & you see another life you could have lived.
structure: Travel between layers is a climb until the ground becomes the sky. No one is carried. Bytopia has no use for passengers.
travel: Gates open in workshops, mine heads, & the moment a job is finished correctly. Idleness is uncomfortable. Magic that cheats labor fizzles.

name: The Sun
inhabitants: Celestial servants who keep the roads through the light. No cities. Only orbits.
overview: The Sun is not a standard heaven in the manuals. On this map it hangs on the left of Elysium, between Bytopia & the Blessed Fields, the day side of the upper rim. That is not the Beastlands' old chair. The wilderness used to sit on Elysium's other side, toward Arborea, & has been pulled into the hub. The Sun is the Daystar given its own throne so noon can live somewhere the hunt no longer holds.
structure: A photosphere of walkable fire, cooler along the mercy roads the archons maintain. Look down & you see the Beastlands as a green coin with a black bite taken out of the east.
travel: Only the fireproof, the invited, or the very foolish. A sending from the Lighthouse can open a mercy road for a few minutes. Do not bring shadow magic. It is eaten.

name: Elysium
inhabitants: Guardinals (leonals, cervidals, equinals) & petitioners who have earned rest. Quiet towns. No walls that look like walls.
overview: Peace so complete it becomes a hazard. Travelers lose the will to leave. The River Oceanus runs through all four layers, & those who drink from it without purpose stay. Elysium is not a trap. It is a home that does not understand why you would want another. On this Wheel the Sun stands to its left. Arborea stands to its right. The Beastlands used to stand on that right hand, between the Blessed Fields & the Olympian Glades, before it was drawn into the hub.
structure: Amoria is meadow & orchard. Eronia is highland. Belierin is marsh, long held against threats the guardinals prefer not to advertise. Thalasia is the sea where the bravest dead go to be unburdened.
travel: The River Oceanus is the surest road from the upper planes. Do not linger in Amoria more than three sleeps. The fourth is how the plane keeps you.

name: Arborea
inhabitants: Elven petitioners, eladrin, satyrs, fey courts, & gods who prefer a feast to a throne. Passion is the local weather.
overview: Arborea feels everything at full volume. Love, wrath, grief, & joy arrive without a governor. The plane is beautiful the way a storm is beautiful. Stay long enough & you will pick a feeling & wear it until it wears you.
structure: Arvandor is forest & vineyard, home of the Seldarine. Aquallor is an ocean that remembers every ship. Mithardir is a white waste of forgotten titans, a reminder that even this plane can burn itself empty.
travel: Gates open at festivals, duels, & the moment a song finishes. Bring a gift. Bring an opinion. Neutrality is considered a kind of rudeness.

name: Ysgard
inhabitants: Petitioners who die well & wake hungry for the next fight. Giants, valkyries, dwarven smiths in the roots. Kord & the Aesir keep halls here.
overview: A plane of broken earthbergs sailing a sky of battle light. Death is a pause. Cowards do not stay. Ysgard loves courage the way a forge loves heat, & it is just as willing to use you up.
structure: The top layer is continents that collide. Muspelheim is volcanic mountain. Nidavellir is cavern & anvil. The three together are one argument about how a life should be spent.
travel: Arrive by falling, climbing, or being thrown. Gates favor mead halls & the moment before a charge. Healing that prevents a glorious scar is considered theft.

name: Mechanus
inhabitants: Modrons in strict hierarchy under Primus. Inevitables who hunt oath breakers. Formians at the edges. Petitioners who lived by procedure.
overview: An infinite orrery. Cogs the size of cities mesh in perfect time. Mechanus is not cruel & it is not kind. It is the idea that the universe should add up. Where it touches other planes, those planes begin to keep appointments.
structure: One layer, endlessly subdivided. The Great Modron March still departs on schedule. When a gear seizes, an inevitable is dispatched.
travel: Gates open at noon exactly, on the second. Late arrivals find brick. Chaos magic misfires into harmless clicking. Bring a written itinerary. The plane will enforce it.

name: The Beastlands
alignmentLong: Neutral Good leaning Chaotic Good campaign hub
inhabitants: Animal lords & their courts, petitioners in beast shape, warden beasts, & the Planesbound companies holding the wall. The hunt continues. It is no longer clean.
overview: The Beastlands is the Outer Plane of the hunt made sacred: not slaughter, the honest contract between hunter & hunted. Three layers keep three lights. Krigala is eternal noon. Brux is eternal dusk. Karasuthra is eternal night. Mortals who stay too long grow fur, or antlers, or a reason to never speak again. On the published Wheel this plane sat between Elysium & Arborea, on Elysium's right, & met the Outlands at the gate town of Faunel. Here the wilderness has been pulled into the hub, where the Outlands ought to sit. Faunel came with it. The Sun did not take the old chair. The Sun sits on Elysium's left.
structure: Krigala is savanna, jungle, & river. Brux is the long red evening of ambush. Karasuthra is the night hunt, where the greatest animal lords keep their thrones. Those three lights are no longer cleanly stacked. They leak.
travel: You are already here. Native gates still open at waterholes, kill sites, & the moment a chase ends honestly. Do not sleep on the eastern bank.

name: The Lighthouse
inhabitants: Planesbound keepers, a small Mechanus embassy, & whoever washes up from the eastern wound at low chaos.
overview: The black & white tower on the Beastlands' eastern headland is a Planesbound holdfast, not a feature from the manuals. It does not warn ships. There are no ships. Its lamp keeps a bearing when the stars over Karasuthra start lying, & when the two overlapping cosmologies refuse to agree on which way is up.
structure: Seven flights, a cistern of river water, & a lantern room whose glass faces the chaos wound on purpose. The keepers call the top floor the Bearing. The lamp is tuned to the Daystar.
travel: Walk the headland road from the inner wall gate, or take the river to the pier if the water is still running downhill. Do not approach during a stutter unless you are expected. From the Bearing you can take a curtain to the Inner Ring & the Will o' Wisp Race.

name: The Ice Wall
alignmentLong: A lawful scar on a wild plane
inhabitants: Planesbound wardens, Bytopian masons, Arcadian surveyors, & whatever hits the ice from the Limbo side & comes through changed.
overview: This is not Beastlands weather. No honest gazetteer gives this plane a glacier ring. The Ice Wall is a made thing: river water, Mechanus cold, & desperate geometry thrown up in a circle to keep the wilderness from dissolving into Limbo.
structure: A sheer pale cliff wrapping the island, inscribed with frost runes that have to be recut after every surge. It is a lattice, not a mountain. Hollows inside hold barracks & rune shops. The ice is thickest on the southern rim.
travel: Inner face gates at the four quarters. The southern postern is safest. Do not climb the outer face during a stutter of the Lighthouse.

name: Limbo
inhabitants: Githzerai monks who hold islands of will, & travelers who thought they could survive on attitude. Most of the last category are weather now.
overview: Limbo is the Outer Plane of pure chaos. Fire, stone, water, & screaming trade identities without asking. A strong mind can hold a bubble of sense for a while. A weak mind becomes a color. This is the raw chaos of the Wheel, & it has never needed an invitation.
structure: No layers that last. Githzerai monasteries are the only reliable landmarks, & they move when their abbots blink. Everything else is soup until someone forces it to be otherwise.
travel: Do not go in unless you can impose order by thought alone, or you have a githzerai guide who owes you a debt. The wound can be entered from the outer ice. That is not a recommendation.

name: Acheron
inhabitants: Armies that outlived their wars. Hobgoblin petitioners, rust dragons, & the occasional god of lost causes. No one here is off duty.
overview: Colossal iron cubes collide in a void the color of old blood. Each face is a battlefield. Victory is real & lasts until the next impact. Acheron is war without a politics, which is to say war with nothing left to pretend about.
structure: Avalas is the clash. Thuldanin is where broken weapons go to become geology. Tintibulus is sterile geometry. Ocanthus is a night of black ice shards that cut identity as cleanly as flesh.
travel: Gates open on parade grounds & in the second before two cubes meet. Bring a banner or be conscripted as scenery.

name: The Nine Hells
inhabitants: Devils in the chain of command, damned petitioners, & anyone who thought they could beat a contract. The hierarchy is the plane.
overview: Nine descending laws. Each layer is a different way to own a soul. The Hells do not waste. They file. They will honor a deal to the letter & starve you on the spirit, & they consider that fairness.
structure: Avernus is the beachhead of the Blood War. Below, cities, swamps, fire, ice, & the pit. Promotion is the only resurrection that matters. Asmodeus still holds Nessus.
travel: Arrive on Avernus unless you enjoy skipping to the part where you owe someone. Contracts signed on plane are enforced by the geography.

name: Gehenna
inhabitants: Yugoloths, petitioners who bargained badly, & nothing that walks without calculating the slope.
overview: Four volcanic mountains hang in a black void, slopes so steep that standing still is a skill. Gehenna is the plane of the cruel deal & the furnace that does not care who you were. Kindness slides off. Literally.
structure: Khalas is lava & factory. Chamada is worse heat. Mungoth mixes ash & snow. Krangath is a mountain that has gone out & taken mercy with it.
travel: Gates open on ledges & in counting houses. Wear spikes. Never accept a hand up without asking what the hand is buying.

name: The Midnight Sun
inhabitants: Nothing that wants a name. A few pilgrims from the Gray Waste come to watch a light die.
overview: The Midnight Sun is not in the manuals. On this campaign map it hangs opposite the Daystar, between Gehenna & Hades, where no sun belongs. It is not an eclipse. An eclipse ends. It is a hole the shape of day, growing in pulses that match the true Sun's dimming.
structure: A photosphere of inverted fire: cold that behaves like heat, darkness that casts a highlight. Walkable along a thin coronal ring. The interior has no agreed depth.
travel: Do not approach during a Lighthouse stutter. The coronal ring can be reached from a Hades side gate. Bring no lantern you hope to keep.

name: Hades
inhabitants: Hordlings, night hags, & petitioners fading toward larva. The Blood War uses Oinos as a board & does not clean up.
overview: The plane that eats color, then motive, then you. Stay long enough & you stop meaning your own name. Hades is not theatrical. It is the argument that nothing was ever worth the effort, delivered as weather.
structure: Oinos is a battlefield of ash & plague. Niflheim is pine mist & surrender. Pluton is the gray orchard where dead kings learn they were not special.
travel: The River Styx is the road, & it is a thief. Bindings, blindfolds, & a reason to leave are mandatory. Anyone who says they feel better here is already lost.

name: Carceri
inhabitants: Titans who lost a war with gods, political prisoners of the Wheel, & anything too useful to kill & too dangerous to free. Demodands keep the keys & do not believe in parole.
overview: Six nested prison orbs. You can always see the next way out. You cannot take it. Carceri is built from the geometry of almost. It holds people who broke a cosmic rule & the ones who were merely in the way.
structure: Each orb sits inside the last. Orthrys is swamp. The layers grow colder, redder, & more personal as you descend. Agathys is a frozen moon with a single citadel & no audience.
travel: Getting in is easy. That is the joke. Getting out requires a sentence completed, a pardon from a power that still claims you, or a lie the plane has not heard. It has heard most of them.

name: The Abyss
inhabitants: Demons without a chain of command that lasts. Tanar'ri, older remnants, & whatever a layer dreamed when it was hungry. The Blood War starts here & never clocks out.
overview: A stacked pit that does not stop. Each layer is a different way to be ruined. The Abyss is not trying to win an argument. It is trying to outlast you. Where Limbo is unshaped, the Abyss is shaped into appetite.
structure: Pazunia is a wasteland of iron fortresses & holes. Below, layers beyond catalog: cities of fungus, seas of acid, personal hells that learned to breed. Maps of the Abyss are boasts.
travel: Pazunia is the only honest arrival. From there, pick a hole & regret it. Binding circles work until they do not. Never accept a guide that smiles with all of its eyes.

name: Pandemonium
inhabitants: Banished things, broken oracles, & petitioners who cannot hear themselves think. The wind is the native. Everything else is a tenant.
overview: An infinite cavern where the wind never stops long enough to be named. Conversation is a skill. Sanity is a resource. Pandemonium is what chaos sounds like when it has walls to scream against.
structure: Pandesmos is the widest tunnels. Cocytus is narrower & crueler. Phlegethon is lightless dripstone. Agathion is sealed chambers that still have something living in them, which is the problem.
travel: Rope, wax for the ears, & a partner who will drag you when you start answering the wind. Gates open in cellars & in the moment a secret is shouted.

name: Far Realms
inhabitants: Not catalogued. Keepers do not staff a post here. Reports disagree with themselves.
overview: ${re} ${ie}
structure: No layers that a Wheel gazetteer can number. Marked on this atlas as a warning, not a road.
travel: There is no honest gate town & no Lighthouse curtain. If you arrive, you did not take a mapped road.

name: Domain of Dread
inhabitants: Darklords who cannot leave, petitioners who think they can, & mists that file both as the same mistake.
structure: Not a rim-plane. A pocket with a warden. Charts that try to number the domains go stale overnight.
travel: Do not take Earth’s road. The mists open for a sin, a relic, or a name spoken twice. Leave by a condition, not a gate.

name: City of Shade
inhabitants: Shade’s clerks, umbral petitioners, & anyone who arrived to disprove a rumor & stayed to file it.
structure: Towers, docks, & a court under a stolen noon. Negative hangs close. The Midnight Sun is the public lie; this is the office.
travel: Arrive only with a death ward & a reason the court should hear you. Prefer the Ethereal curtain-road. Do not follow a dock-light that has no lamp.

name: Miskatonic
inhabitants: Keepers who file anomalies, student clerks who should not have keys, & specimens that learned the catalog numbers.
structure: Upper stacks for the gazetteer. A locked basement for SCP work: contain, describe, & do not demonstrate. The Digital Void is a sister schism, not a reading room.
travel: From the Lighthouse, a clean Daystar pulse can open a clerk’s door. Bring a lamp. Do not take a souvenir. The basement does not check books out.

name: BEYOND
epithet: More Wheels than one pair of eyes can see..
alignmentLong: More Wheels than one pair of eyes can see..
inhabitants: Wizards who overlay Wheels, dreamers who wake in the wrong edition, & keepers who treat the HUD as a tool, not a god.
structure: Not a rim-plane. A viewing-room. The Dreamlands sit behind the glass. Limbo is the nearest wound if the HUD fails.
travel: Tune a Compass Orb, then a wizard’s HUD, when the Daystar pulse is clean. Walk the Ethereal curtain if the overlay starts counting extra moons.

name: Lumia
inhabitants: Oathbound who keep both facets, pact-wrights who work in glare, & surveyors of celestial angles who will not pick a single heaven.
structure: A celestial lattice, not a mountain. Frozen Oath holds one face. Burning Pact holds the other. The Daystar is a neighbor, not a landlord.
travel: From the Lighthouse, take a clean Daystar bearing toward the Sun’s gap. Do not swear both vows in the same breath.
